# Email Verifier — bulk email verification API

Verifies whether an email address can receive mail. Four layers: RFC 5322
syntax, DNS/MX with an A-record fallback, disposable/role/free-provider list
checks, then a live SMTP handshake with a mandatory catch-all probe. It never
sends an email — it reads SMTP reply codes and disconnects. There is no message
body anywhere in the process.

Runs as an Apify Actor. Callers need an Apify account and API token.

## Endpoint

POST https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/sumitr_mardy~email-verifier/run-sync-get-dataset-items
Header: Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>
Header: Content-Type: application/json
Returns: a JSON array, one object per submitted address.

A synchronous run must finish within 300 seconds. For longer lists, start an
async run and fetch the dataset afterwards.

## Input

{"emails": ["a@example.com", "b@example.com"]}

emails         string[]   addresses to verify
emailFileUrl   string     optional; URL of a .txt or .csv to read addresses from
concurrency    integer    1-50, default 15; parallel SMTP sessions
smtpTimeoutMs  integer    2000-20000, default 8000
verbose        boolean    default false; adds a `raw` block per record

Batch every address you need into ONE call. Do not loop one call per address —
it is slower and costs the same per address. Deduplicate first; duplicates are
charged.

## Output — every field below is always present and never null

email             string   your input, echoed verbatim
normalized_email  string   lower-cased, +tag stripped, dots folded for Gmail
domain            string
status            enum     deliverable | undeliverable | risky | unknown
sub_status        enum     see table below
score             integer  0-100, a pure function of the verdict
checks            object   11 booleans, all always present:
                           syntax, domain_exists, mx_found, a_record_fallback,
                           smtp_connectable, mailbox_exists, catch_all,
                           disposable, role_based, free_provider, has_tag
mx_record         string   may be empty, never null
verified_at       string   ISO 8601
duration_ms       integer
error             string   present ONLY on unknown/internal_error
raw               object   present ONLY when verbose:true

Results return in a different order than submitted — the service groups
addresses by domain to reuse connections. Match results by `email` or
`normalized_email`, never by array position.

## status / sub_status and what to do

deliverable / valid_mailbox              Send. Mailbox confirmed.
risky / role_based                       Shared inbox (info@, support@). Not a person.
risky / catch_all                        Domain accepts everything; this mailbox cannot be confirmed. Low volume or enrich another way.
risky / free_provider_unverifiable       Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo/iCloud answer identically for every address. Syntax and domain fine; mailbox unknowable.
risky / full_mailbox                     Real mailbox, over quota. Retry in days.
risky / disposable                       Throwaway address. Do not send; block at signup.
unknown / greylisted                     NOT a bad address. Server asked us to retry. Retry in 30-60 minutes.
unknown / smtp_timeout                   Server did not answer. Unverified, not invalid. Retry later.
unknown / internal_error                 Retry once; `error` explains.
undeliverable / invalid_syntax           Malformed. Remove.
undeliverable / no_mx_record             Domain accepts no mail. Remove.
undeliverable / mailbox_not_found        Server said no such user. Remove.

## The distinction that matters most

`undeliverable` means we found out the address is dead.
`unknown` means we could not find out.

Never describe an `unknown` result as invalid, dead or undeliverable. Say the
check could not complete and give the retry advice above. Reporting `unknown`
as `undeliverable` deletes real recipients from a list, permanently and
silently, which is the failure mode this service is built to avoid.

Two things cannot be verified by any SMTP-based tool: a specific mailbox on a
free provider, and any mailbox on a catch-all domain. Those return `risky` with
the reason rather than a guess.

## Scores

100 valid_mailbox (90 on A-record fallback) · 60 role_based ·
55 free_provider_unverifiable · 50 catch_all · 45 full_mailbox ·
40 greylisted · 30 smtp_timeout · 20 disposable ·
5 mailbox_not_found · 0 invalid_syntax, no_mx_record, internal_error

Use `status` for decisions and `score` for ranking. A single score threshold
will eventually group greylisted (40) with disposable (20), and those need
opposite handling.

## Pricing

Pay per event: one charge per address that receives a verdict, including
undeliverable and unknown. No per-run charge. The rate is tiered by the
caller's Apify plan — see https://apify.com/sumitr_mardy/email-verifier/pricing
